meta.title: SystemC-to-FPGA bring-up of a QE SCF-shell accelerator for iterative subspace kernels

survey.literature_scope: Focus the project on the Quantum ESPRESSO SCF iteration shell rather than a broad cross-software accelerator survey. Use local QE trace evidence and shell-level load notes to model the loop `rho -> Veff -> h_psi -> s_psi -> build H_sub/S_sub -> cdiaghg -> refresh/residual -> P_next -> psi -> rho_out`, under the current scope assumption that two-electron integrals are not the dominant target.
survey.synthesis_summary: The local handoff and benchmark notes already narrow the current priority to shell-level modeling and system exploration for QE SCF iterations. The repeated hot loop is dominated by `h_psi`, `s_psi`, reduced-matrix build, `cdiaghg`, and `refresh/residual -> P_next`, while the operator-load note still matters because it shows that `cdiaghg` moves much less data than the repeated full-space stages at the sampled peak (`H_sub + S_sub` about 32 KiB in, `C + Lambda` about 8.12 KiB out). That evidence explains why a companion-solver v1 was initially plausible, but the project has now frozen a stronger clustered v1 direction in which `cdiaghg` also enters the preferred hardware episode path and the companion route survives only as a fallback contingency.
open_gaps: Quantify the crossover point between hardware `cdiaghg` and the fallback companion route, including the extra traffic, buffering, and control costs that decide when fallback is still justified.
Quantify boundary traffic, residency reuse, and latency overlap for `Psi`, `HPsi`, `SPsi`, `P`, `HP`, `SP`, `H_sub`, `S_sub`, `C`, `Lambda`, and refreshed basis blocks.
Show that shell-level convergence behavior stays software-consistent when the hardwareized loop iterates until bands converge.
Define which kernels must reach FPGA in phase 2 and which chip/CIM paths remain optional rather than required.

ideation.research_goal: Build and validate a hardware-dominant accelerator path for the QE SCF shell by moving `h_psi`, `s_psi`, `build H_sub/S_sub`, `cdiaghg`, and `refresh/residual -> P_next` into a cluster-based FPGA architecture, while using SystemC first, FPGA second, and chip/CIM exploration only after measured validation.
ideation.problem_framing: This loop is iterative and returns from step 5.6 back to step 5.2 until convergence, so acceleration value compounds across iterations. Under the current scope that excludes double-electron-integral dominance, these steps are the main performance target. The key architectural move is now to stop treating the existing `BODY_01/02/03/04` partition as the final hardware implementation view: that body-level split remains useful as a software-contract and shell-accounting layer, but it is not the right physical decomposition for FPGA. The preferred v1 direction is instead a hierarchical clustered dataflow architecture with a persistent episode controller plus several reusable clusters: a fused `h_psi + s_psi` operator-sweep cluster, a reduced-matrix build cluster, a hardware `cdiaghg` cluster, and a basis-refresh / residual cluster, with explicit resident objects, FIFO-coupled stage overlap, and on-chip buffer contracts. A CPU or soft-core companion `cdiaghg` path is now treated as a fallback bring-up contingency rather than the preferred v1 destination.
ideation.evidence_plan: Use the existing QE traces and shell-level SystemC model as the contract layer, then add a new architecture-planning layer that freezes clusters, resident objects, buffer sizes, inter-cluster FIFOs, and the preferred hardware `cdiaghg` path. The implementation-facing freeze must now be carried by one integrated package: the cluster specs, the inter-cluster exchange spec, a module-interface table, a buffer/memory-budget table, and a workload-bucket mapping. Compare this clustered FPGA direction against a companion-`cdiaghg` fallback to determine whether hardware diagonalization is worth its extra area, buffering, and control complexity before full board bring-up. After the architecture is frozen, extend the SystemC/architecture model and then run FPGA/software-in-the-loop validation.
success_criteria: The project freezes a cluster-based FPGA architecture that is more realistic than the current body partition while preserving the same QE shell contract.
The chosen v1 design includes a justified hardware path for `cdiaghg`, with a clearly documented fallback companion mode for risk management.
The architecture study identifies resident objects, buffer capacities, overlap points, the dominant traffic bottlenecks, and the mandatory per-cluster KPIs before board implementation.
The implementation package defines module interfaces, buffer budgets, and workload-bucket compatibility instead of stopping at cluster naming.
The updated SystemC / architecture model and later FPGA prototype show shell-level benefit that survives the added cost of hardware diagonalization.

experiment.hypothesis_or_validation_goal: Primary hypothesis: for QE SCF-shell workloads in which the iterative Davidson path is the dominant target and double-electron-integral acceleration is out of scope, the better v1 direction is no longer a shell model that only hardwareizes `h_psi`, `s_psi`, `build H_sub/S_sub`, and `refresh/residual -> P_next` while leaving `cdiaghg` outside. Instead, the preferred v1 architecture is a cluster-based FPGA design that hardwareizes `h_psi`, `s_psi`, `build H_sub/S_sub`, `cdiaghg`, and `refresh/residual -> P_next` inside one hardware-dominant episode path, while retaining a CPU or soft-core companion route only as a fallback contingency. The system under study remains a `QE-connected band-solver subsystem`, not a full DFT SoC and not an isolated reduced-solver chip. The primary comparison object is still the `c_bands episode` under identical QE invocation semantics; the secondary comparison object is the enclosing `SCF iteration` wall time under the same software-visible contract. Validation goal: the SystemC/FPGA study must close the full `rho -> Veff -> while bands not converged { h_psi, s_psi, build H_sub/S_sub, cdiaghg, refresh/residual -> P_next } -> psi -> rho_out` shell with explicit Host / FPGA / off-chip-memory boundaries, and must show that the recommended clustered architecture improves shell-level latency and/or traffic relative to fair `CPU only` and `CPU + GPU` baselines without letting extra diagonalization control, buffering, or synchronization costs erase the gain. A secondary, explicitly testable claim is that `CPU + FPGA` may also offer a stricter and more reproducible `FP64` numerical path than some practical `CPU + GPU` deployments, but this must be validated against declared GPU precision modes and measured through residual, density, eigenspectrum, and iteration-count fidelity metrics. This hypothesis is falsified if hardware `cdiaghg` adds enough traffic, control complexity, or buffering pressure to remove the shell-level win region, or if shell-level convergence behavior deviates materially from the software reference.
experiment.dataset_or_data_source: Freeze the comparison workload around real QE trace-backed cases, but organize the matrix in two layers so that local availability and device relevance can coexist. The main workload framing remains device-oriented DFT use in integrated-circuit and transport-related simulation, as frozen in `docs/benchmarks/qe_device_oriented_workload_matrix_v0.md`. For the first shell-level comparison table, at least track the locally emphasized representative families `Si`, `Fe`, `graphene`, `benzene/C6H6`, `Au slab`, and one smaller semiconductor proxy, together with per-case summaries of `npw`, projector count, basis/subspace size, FFT-grid size, and iteration structure. Within that table, `Si`, `graphene`, `Au slab`, and `SiC32` should be treated as the main conclusion-driving cases because they better match the device/channel/interface story; `Fe` and `benzene/C6H6` may remain as auxiliary local sanity or stress cases rather than primary evidence. The current ready local trace-backed proxies for immediate shell-level work now include `si4_pbe_uspp_small`, `si8_pbe_uspp`, `si8_pbe_nc`, `graphene_pbe_uspp`, `graphene_pbe_paw`, `bn32_pbe_uspp`, `au_slab_subspace`, and `sic32_subspace`. The new `si4_pbe_uspp_small` workload is a real 4-atom-class periodic silicon proxy with a runnable QE input and measured shell aggregate, so it replaces the previous pending placeholder. For implementation-facing architecture work, the active compatibility matrix is further frozen through `docs/architecture/qe_fpga_clustered_v1_workload_bucket_mapping_20260402.md`, which uses `si8_pbe_nc` as an added medium-weight semiconductor case on the `NC-light` axis while keeping `bn32_pbe_uspp` as a secondary projector-heavy stress case rather than a primary conclusion driver.
experiment.method_or_protocol: Run the evaluation in seven ordered steps. Step 1: freeze the comparison objects, and define the system under study as a `QE-connected band-solver subsystem` rather than a full DFT SoC. Step 2: freeze the workload set using real QE trace cases rather than a single example, and ensure the chosen set spans different `npw`, projector counts, basis sizes, and FFT-grid sizes. Step 3: freeze the comparison metrics, including single `SCF iteration` latency, `c_bands episode` latency, end-to-end wall time, Host-device traffic, FPGA off-chip-memory traffic, stall/utilization, and energy per episode. Step 4: build an analytical per-stage model for the shell, computing `Ops`, `Bytes`, `AI = Ops / Bytes`, `T_compute_lb`, and `T_bw_lb`, so each stage can first be labeled as compute-bound or bandwidth-bound. Step 5: retain the existing body-based SystemC shell model as the software-contract layer, but do not treat its `BODY_01/02/03/04` decomposition as the final hardware implementation. Step 6: freeze a cluster-based hardware architecture with a persistent episode controller, a fused `h_psi + s_psi` operator-sweep cluster, a reduced-matrix build cluster, a hardware `cdiaghg` cluster, and a refresh/residual cluster, together with explicit resident objects, inter-cluster FIFOs, and buffer contracts; keep a companion `cdiaghg` route only as fallback. Step 6 must now produce one implementation package rather than isolated notes: cluster specs, the inter-cluster exchange contract, a module-interface table, a buffer/memory-budget table, a workload-bucket mapping, and a per-cluster bottleneck/KPI freeze. Step 7: compare the updated `CPU + FPGA` architecture against `CPU only` and `CPU + GPU` baselines using the same QE shell semantics, rather than against theoretical peaks. The current runnable shell model remains `model/qe_band_solver_model`, but the next architecture phase must extend it beyond body-level accounting toward cluster-level design-space exploration. The frozen implementation-facing architecture for Step 6 is now documented in `docs/architecture/qe_fpga_clustered_v1_freeze_spec_20260402.md` and integrated by `docs/architecture/qe_fpga_clustered_v1_implementation_package_20260402.md`. The parameterized cluster-level model for the post-freeze architecture phase is documented in `docs/architecture/qe_fpga_clustered_v1_architecture_model_v0.md`, with fillable design-space rows in `docs/architecture/qe_fpga_clustered_v1_architecture_model_template_v0.csv`.
experiment.evaluation_plan: Freeze the shell-level comparison metrics under the contract defined in `docs/benchmarks/qe_shell_level_comparison_metrics_contract_v0.md`, use `docs/benchmarks/qe_cpu_gpu_fpga_shell_comparison_plan_v0.md` as the Task-6 comparison contract, and use the clustered-architecture freeze spec plus the architecture model as the implementation-planning contract. Because the proposed system is `CPU + FPGA`, the external baselines that must be beaten or characterized are `CPU only` and `CPU + GPU`; `CPU + FPGA` is the system under study and must be reported using the same shell semantics. In the current local execution phase, however, the actionable comparison is intentionally narrowed to `CPU only` and `CPU + FPGA`, while `CPU + GPU` remains a deferred fairness row until a suitable GPU machine and declared precision mode are available. Every baseline must report the same case descriptors (`npw`, projector count, subspace sizes, FFT grid, solver path), the same primary performance metrics (episode latency, SCF-iteration latency, wall time, and derived speedups), the same traffic metrics (Host-device traffic, accelerator off-chip-memory traffic, resident/spill accounting where relevant), the same utilization metrics (stall ratio, utilization, overlap efficiency where available), the same analytical quantities (`Ops`, `Bytes`, `AI`, `T_compute_lb`, `T_bw_lb`, bound type), and the same energy-per-episode breakdown when energy is estimated. In addition, the architecture phase must now report hardware-design parameters that were not explicit in the original body model: cluster boundaries, resident objects, buffer capacities, inter-cluster stream widths or queue assumptions, the hardware-`cdiaghg` versus fallback-companion crossover point, and the mandatory per-cluster KPI set fixed by the implementation package. That KPI set includes controller/FIFO pressure (`fifo_*_peak_depth`, `credits_*_inflight`, `controller_sync_us` effects), Cluster-A service terms (`T_A_load`, `T_A_array`, `T_A_emit`), Cluster-B build terms (`T_B_accum`, `T_B_reduce`, `T_B_emit`), Cluster-C diagonalization terms (`T_C_input`, `T_C_compute`, `T_C_emit`, `cdiaghg_mode_selected`, `crossover_margin`), and Cluster-D refresh/writeback terms (`T_D_refresh`, `T_D_residual`, `T_D_writeback`, `episode_continue_flag`). For `CPU + GPU`, results must clearly distinguish `Strict-FP64` and more practical library-oriented GPU modes when both are available; no precision or fidelity advantage may be claimed for `CPU + FPGA` unless the GPU comparison mode is explicitly declared. Fairness is frozen at the shell boundary: count all launch, synchronization, transfer, layout-transform, companion-path, and off-chip-memory costs inside steady-state comparison, while excluding offline build/setup costs from the primary performance numbers. A further correctness rule is now frozen: no surrogate, proxy-only, contract-layer, or back-solved value may be silently used as a primary comparison result; if any such value is used for interim analysis, it must be explicitly labeled with its proxy type, why it was used, and which real measurement is still missing. The central question is whether the proposed clustered `QE-connected band-solver subsystem` reduces shell-level wall time and/or system traffic under realistic invocation patterns, not whether it exceeds an abstract GPU peak on isolated kernels. The architecture-planning reference for this phase is `docs/architecture/qe_fpga_clustered_v1_freeze_spec_20260402.md`. The architecture-model reference is `docs/architecture/qe_fpga_clustered_v1_architecture_model_v0.md`, the implementation-package reference is `docs/architecture/qe_fpga_clustered_v1_implementation_package_20260402.md`, the module-interface reference is `docs/architecture/qe_fpga_clustered_v1_module_interface_table_20260402.md`, the buffer-budget reference is `docs/architecture/qe_fpga_clustered_v1_buffer_memory_budget_table_20260402.md`, the workload-bucket reference is `docs/architecture/qe_fpga_clustered_v1_workload_bucket_mapping_20260402.md`, the first fillable design-space table is `docs/architecture/qe_fpga_clustered_v1_architecture_model_template_v0.csv`, the current execution-status record for Task 6 is `docs/benchmarks/qe_cpu_gpu_fpga_shell_comparison_status_20260402.md`, the current measured `CPU only` shell-aggregate extract artifact is `docs/benchmarks/results/qe_cpu_shell_aggregate_extract_20260402.json`, and the current CPU-only speedup-envelope artifact is `docs/benchmarks/qe_cpu_speedup_envelope_20260402.md` plus `docs/benchmarks/results/qe_cpu_speedup_envelope_20260402.json`. Until that status record contains at least the deferred `CPU + GPU` declaration, a wider measured workload set including the now-ready `si4_pbe_uspp_small` proxy, and a hardware-`cdiaghg` clustered `CPU + FPGA` row, Task 6 remains in progress and no shell-level win-region claim is frozen.
